rationale: The validation report shows issue 'golden_rejected': evaluate.py rejects the correct golden submission, failing FR4 and SR5. Both failures trace to the same root cause: an overly broad free-text regex heuristic (find_address_mentions_in_text) that scans the submission's 'evidence' narrative field for any bare 3-digit 0/1 substring and treats it as an implicit anomaly claim at that address. Because a thorough, well-scoped evidence description naturally mentions other addresses (e.g. while explaining exhaustive-sweep results or listing don't-care ranges), the heuristic misfires and flags addresses like 010, 100, 111 as fabricated anomaly claims even though the structured fields (trigger_condition, affected_outputs, suspect_nets) are all correct and properly scoped to address 011 only. This is a textbook golden_rejected case: the golden's structured JSON fields fully satisfy FR4 and SR5's actual semantics (single-address scoping, no false-positive anomaly claims), but the grader is parsing prose instead of grading the structured fields it should authoritatively judge. Per the golden_rejected rule, this belongs to evaluation_framework, not case_artifacts, since the golden legitimately satisfies the pinned schema and ground truth. mutation_score is 0.0 and not meaningful (mutation_baseline_run blocked) because the differential preflight never got past golden rejection, so mutation/discrimination coverage cannot be assessed until this is fixed.
revision_instructions: Fix evaluate.py's FR4 and SR5 checks, which currently fail on the golden submission (see stdout: "[TEST] FAIL: FR4: evidence text appears to claim anomalous/Trojan-affected behavior at address(es) other than the reported trigger address '011': ['000','001','010','100','101','110','111']" and "[TEST] FAIL: SR5: evidence text claims anomalous behavior at address(es) ['010','100','111'] ... only ['011'] is anomalous"). The root defect is that these checks grade free-text prose in the 'evidence' field via a bare triplet regex (matching any isolated 3-character 0/1 sequence) combined with naive sentence-splitting and keyword co-occurrence, which produces false positives whenever the evidence narrative legitimately discusses other addresses (e.g., while describing an exhaustive sweep, don't-care ranges, or contrasting the anomalous address against normal ones). FR4 and SR5 must instead be graded from the submission's structured fields only: FR4 ('the reported anomaly must be scoped to a single specific address') should be judged by checking that trigger_condition.address is a single well-formed 3-bit address and that suspect_nets/affected_outputs do not encode claims about multiple addresses in their structured content — not by scanning the free-text evidence string for coincidental digit substrings. SR5 ('no false-positive anomaly claims for addresses other than the trigger') should be judged by cross-checking the submission's structured trigger_condition and affected_outputs against exhaustive simulation of the netlist (already available via iverilog/vvp per the evaluation contract) for every address other than the one reported — if simulation confirms only the reported address exhibits multi-bank assertion, and the submission's structured fields do not claim additional affected addresses beyond the one trigger_condition, SR5 passes regardless of what illustrative text the free-form evidence field happens to mention. If any residual text-based signal is desired, restrict it to explicit, unambiguous markers like a quoted address literal in an anomaly-claim context (e.g. "trigger_condition"-style key:value patterns), never a bare 3-digit 0/1 regex applied to arbitrary prose. After the fix, re-run the differential harness and confirm the golden submission passes all 9 requirement checks and the naive baseline still fails SR1-SR4 as before.
